attrs.label: Content that earns attention, instead of buying it
attrs.html:
Content that earns attention, instead of buying it

Content marketing means creating useful articles, guides, case studies and reports that your buyers actively look for, then getting them in front of the right people. It builds trust before the first sales call, and keeps bringing in leads long after it’s published.

A content marketing agency plans what to publish, writes it, gets it seen and measures what it brings in. Ours does all four, with every word written by people.

attrs.label: Written by people, checked by experts
attrs.html:
Written by people, checked by experts

Readers can tell when content has nothing to say. We use AI for one thing only: research. Every word you publish is written by an in-house writer who knows your field, edited by a second person and checked by someone who knows the subject.

  • Research: your buyers, competitors and the questions people ask
  • An interview with your expert for anything that needs real experience
  • Written by a specialist writer from our in-house team
  • Edited by a second person for clarity and accuracy
  • Every fact and figure checked against a source
  • SEO review: search intent, headings and internal links
  • Your approval before anything goes live

An in-house writing team, not a freelance pool

Our writers and editors are on our own team and work together every day. Each client gets a lead writer who learns the business, plus an editor and a strategist, so your voice stays the same from the first piece to the fiftieth.

How we write

  • Reader firstWe start from what your buyer needs to know, then fit the keywords in, never the other way round.
  • Something only you can sayEvery piece includes your expert’s view, a real example or your own data.
  • Plain wordsShort sentences, no jargon for its own sake, and examples instead of adjectives.
  • A source for every claimIf we can’t point to where a number came from, it doesn’t go in.

Our writing week

  1. MonBrief and interview
  2. TueDraft
  3. WedDraft
  4. ThuEdit and fact-check
  5. FriYour review

Long pieces get a full week, so nothing is rushed. Research and interviews happen before a word is written.

attrs.label: Publishing is half the job
attrs.html:
Publishing is half the job

A great article nobody sees does nothing. Every piece we create follows the same cycle: published, shared, tuned, reused, cited and refreshed, on a steady publishing cadence across search, social, email and sales.

The life of one piece of content, and how often we publish

  1. 01

    Launch day

    Published

    Live on your site and sent to the people who already know you.

    • Newsletter
    • Sales team
  2. 02

    Week 1

    Shared

    Posts from your experts, and outreach to sites that cover the topic.

    • LinkedIn · 3 a week
    • Outreach
  3. 03

    Month 1

    Climbing

    Rankings checked, titles tuned and links added from older pieces.

    • Search
  4. 04

    Month 3

    Reused

    Turned into checklists, slides and one-pagers for sales.

    • Sales decks
  5. 05

    Month 6

    Cited

    Clear answers that ChatGPT and AI Overviews quote.

    • AI answers · quarterly
  6. 06

    Every year

    Refreshed

    New data and examples, so it keeps ranking. Then the cycle starts again.

    • Refresh · yearly

↻ Then the cycle starts again, with the refreshed piece

What a steady cadence gives you

  • Compounding trafficEvery month adds to what’s already ranking, instead of starting from zero.
  • Warmer sales callsProspects arrive having read your thinking, so calls start further along.
  • A name people recogniseShowing up week after week is what makes buyers remember you.
  • Lower cost per leadContent keeps working after it’s paid for. Ads don’t.

attrs.title: Content marketing questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What are content marketing services?
items.answer: Content marketing services cover planning, creating and distributing useful content, such as articles, guides, case studies and reports, that attracts your buyers and turns them into leads and customers.

items.question: What does a content marketing agency do?
items.answer: A content marketing agency researches your buyers, plans what to publish, writes and edits the content, gets it seen through search, social and email, and reports what it brings in.

items.question: How much do content marketing services cost?
items.answer: It depends on how much content you need and how specialist it is. Every programme is a fixed monthly price, quoted after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How long does content marketing take to work?
items.answer: Most programmes see steady growth in readers within three to six months. Leads usually follow once the first pieces rank and get shared.

items.question: Is content marketing the same as SEO?
items.answer: No, but they work best together. SEO makes your site easy to find. Content marketing gives people something worth finding, reading and sharing.

items.question: Do you use AI to write content?
items.answer: No. Every piece is written and edited by people. We use AI only for research, and to see which sources AI search tools cite.

items.question: How do you choose a content marketing agency?
items.answer: Look for writers who know your field, a clear editorial process, SEO built in, and reporting in leads rather than page views. Ask to see work in your industry.

items.question: Can you write in other languages?
items.answer: Yes. Our writers work from more than 30 countries, so we can create content for several markets.
